lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 20: RBAC and ServiceAccounts
lesson.description: Give a Pod its own identity, grant it exactly the API access it needs with Roles and bindings, and check every permission with kubectl auth can-i.
lesson.tested: Roles, bindings, can-i, Pod tokens and API calls tested on kind v0.33.0, node v1.37.0, 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Nothing is allowed until a binding says so. Give each workload its own ServiceAccount, grant the smallest Role that works, and prove it with kubectl auth can-i before you ship.

cheatsheet.intro: Who, what, which, where, and the commands from Lesson 20.

rows.name: Role
rows.role: Rules in one namespace: apiGroups, resources and verbs. An empty apiGroup is the core group.

rows.name: ClusterRole
rows.role: The same rules, not namespaced. Use it for nodes, or reuse view, edit and admin.

rows.name: RoleBinding
rows.role: Grants a Role or a ClusterRole inside one namespace. roleRef is immutable.

rows.name: ClusterRoleBinding
rows.role: Grants a ClusterRole everywhere. It cannot reference a Role.

rows.name: Before a binding
rows.role: The Pod's call to list Pods returned 403. can-i list pods answered no.

rows.name: pod-reader
rows.role: After the RoleBinding, the same call listed Pods. delete, other namespaces, Services and nodes stayed no.

rows.name: view
rows.role: A RoleBinding to the view ClusterRole allowed Services in this namespace, not in kube-system, and not Secrets.

rows.name: Token
rows.role: The mounted token's warnafter is 3607 seconds after iat. create token --duration=10m is a 600 second token. automountServiceAccountToken false mounts no token.

items.what: kubectl auth whoami shows the subject. Add --as to ask about a ServiceAccount.
A Role for deployments with apiGroups empty answered no. apps/v1 means the group is apps. After that change, can-i answered yes.
A binding with --serviceaccount=default:helper grants helper in default, not in k8s-from-zero. get rolebinding -o wide shows default/helper.
Permissions only add up. There are no deny rules.

commands.cmd: kubectl auth can-i list pods -n k8s-from-zero --as=system:serviceaccount:k8s-from-zero:inspector

commands.note: which group a resource lives in

homework.intro: Use the kind cluster from part 3 and the namespace k8s-from-zero. The lesson's ServiceAccount is inspector. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: What does a Role hold, and what does a RoleBinding add?
exercises.a: A Role holds rules: apiGroups, resources and verbs, in one namespace. A RoleBinding says who gets those rules, and where. A RoleBinding can also point at a ClusterRole and still grant it only in the binding's namespace.

exercises.q: Why does view not include Secrets?
exercises.a: Reading Secrets would expose ServiceAccount tokens and other credentials. view is a ClusterRole meant to be bound per namespace.

exercises.q: What does automountServiceAccountToken: false change, and which setting wins?
exercises.a: The Pod gets no token, ca.crt or namespace file. The Pod setting wins over the same field on the ServiceAccount. The Pod still runs as that ServiceAccount.

exercises.q: Before any binding, run can-i list pods as inspector, and have the Pod call the API. What did the lesson record?
exercises.a: can-i answered no. The API call returned 403 Forbidden. After pod-reader was applied, the same call listed the Pods.

exercises.q: Decode the mounted token the way the lesson does. What do exp, iat and warnafter say?
exercises.a: exp is about a year after iat, because admission extends the injected token. warnafter is 3607 seconds after iat, the real lifetime in the projected volume. kubectl create token --duration=10m gives a token whose lifetime is 600 seconds.

exercises.q: Create a Role for deployments with apiGroups set to the empty string. What does can-i say, and what fixes it?
exercises.a: no. kubectl api-resources shows deployments in apps/v1. Set apiGroups to apps and the same check answers yes.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: You edit a RoleBinding's roleRef to point at a different Role. What does the API do?
exercises.a: It rejects the change. roleRef is immutable. Delete the binding and create a new one.

exercises.q: A ClusterRoleBinding's roleRef kind is Role. What error does the lesson quote?
exercises.a: roleRef.kind: Unsupported value Role. Supported value: ClusterRole. A ClusterRoleBinding can only reference a ClusterRole.

exercises.q: The binding says helper, and can-i still says no. What does the lesson tell you to look at?
exercises.a: The subject's namespace. --serviceaccount=default:helper grants helper in default. kubectl get rolebinding -o wide shows default/helper. The ServiceAccount in k8s-from-zero is a different subject.
